chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Hashim ibn Yahya al-Mada'ini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) went to a water container and drank from it while he was standing.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful — the title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.إِدَاوَة: A small leather vessel or water flask used for carrying and drinking water
key_terms.قَائِم: Standing, upright — describing the posture during drinking

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to drink water while standing in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him), the Commander of the Faithful, drank water from a leather flask (idawa) while standing upright. This narration appears in a chapter addressing the ruling on drinking while standing, providing prophetic precedent that permits this practice. The act is attributed to Imam Ali to establish that drinking while standing is not categorically prohibited in Shia jurisprudence, countering some Sunni traditions that discourage it.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Hashim Bin Yahya Al Madainy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> had a water container, so he<sup>asws</sup> drank from it and he<sup>asws</sup> was standing’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ali from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Hashim [from abu Hashim] ibn Yahya al-Mada’iniy who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin went to the water container and drank water standing.’”
